newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks stage late recovery to close higher.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks stage late recovery to close higher.

text.p: Mexican stocks surged in late trading Thursday, reversing an early slump to end higher amid bargain-hunting.
"Buyers mobbed the market at the close. Telmex, which was in demand from midday onwards, and blue chips gave the bourse a second wind," a trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 24.45 points, or 0.64 percent, at 3,821.75. The IPC had dropped to an early low of 3,764.77 points at midday following weak U.S. stock and bond markets.
Telecommunications firm Telmex L shares rallied to close up 32 centavos (4 cents) at 16.20 pesos ($2.05), while its ADRs bucked the lower trend on Wall Street to gain 1/2 to 40-7/8.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 23.79 points at 6,540.05.
In Mexico, retail chain Cifra's three share series topped the prominent gainers' list at brisk volume.

The A shares climbed 56 centavos (7 cents) to 11.56 pesos ($1.46), the C class gained 46 centavos (6 cents) to 11.56 pesos ($1.46). Cifra's B shares, which are more actively traded, rose 44 centavos (6 cents) to 11.64 pesos ($1.47).
Volume was unremarkable at 74.2 million shares.
The broad market did not reflect gains in blue chips. Of 101 stocks traded, 46 ended down while 31 were up.
Retail group Salinas and Rocha notched up strong gains for the fifth straight day amid market speculation of an asset sale to improve the company's finances.
"There is talk of an assets sale, but there would be no change in the control of the firm as it is only L class shares that have moved, which have no voting rights," a trader said.
Salinas y Rocha gained 14 centavos (2 cents) to 80 centavos (10 cents).

Congolmerate Grupo Sidek headed the list of prominent decliners, down two centavos (less than 1 cent) to 34 centavos (4 cents) after a shareholders' assembly did not dispel concerns about the debt-ridden company's future, traders said.
